requirements.text: This Request for Proposals ("RFP") sets out the background and objectives of the assignment, the scope of work, the mandatory eligibility criteria, the technical and functional requirements, the evaluation criteria and methodology, the submission instructions, and the principal commercial terms that will govern the resulting contract.
At present, citizens of the Province must visit multiple departmental offices in person to obtain certificates, licences, permits and registrations.
For the purposes of this RFP, the following definitions shall apply:
The successful Bidder shall design, build, test, deploy, operate and maintain the Provincial e-Services Citizen Portal as a turnkey solution.
The Bidder shall be responsible for end-to-end delivery, including project management, quality assurance, information security compliance and warranty support, for the duration of the Contract.
The Portal shall provide a single point of access for citizens, businesses and government users.

It shall offer account registration and login using CNIC-based identity verification, a personalised citizen dashboard, application submission with document upload, real-time application status tracking, electronic payment of fees and taxes, downloadable digitally signed certificates, and a grievance redressal module.

The entire public-facing experience shall be fully bilingual in Urdu and English, including right-to-left rendering for Urdu content, and shall conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility requirements.
The Portal must be responsive across desktop, tablet and smartphone form factors and must function correctly on low-bandwidth connections of 256 kbps or better.
3.3 e-Services Catalogue The Bidder shall digitise, configure and operate no fewer than forty (40) e-services in consultation with the participating departments.

Each e-service shall be implemented with a configurable workflow engine supporting multi-step approvals, delegations, escalations, automatic SMS and email notifications at every state change, and service-level timers aligned with the Provincial Citizens Charter.

The System shall integrate with at least two licensed payment aggregators operating in Pakistan and shall support payment through debit and credit cards, internet and mobile banking (including 1LINK and RAAST rails), over-the-counter bank challans with barcode, and mobile wallets.
The System shall generate PSID-based challans reconcilable with the provincial treasury, shall perform automated daily reconciliation, and shall provide a refunds and chargeback handling workflow.
All payment flows must be PCI DSS compliant to the extent applicable to the integration model adopted.
The Bidder shall deliver native or cross-platform mobile applications for Android (minimum Android 9) and iOS (minimum iOS 14), published under the Authority's developer accounts.

The mobile applications shall provide functional parity with the Portal for at least the twenty (20) highest-volume services, shall support biometric login, push notifications, offline draft saving, and in-app payment, and shall be fully bilingual in Urdu and English.

The Bidder shall plan and execute the migration of records from the legacy departmental systems described in Annex D, which include: (a) the District Records Management System operating on Oracle 11g with approximately 9.2 million records;

The Bidder shall be responsible for data profiling, cleansing rules, de-duplication, transformation, migration rehearsal runs, reconciliation reports with record-level audit trails, and sign-off of migration completeness with each data-owning department.
Legacy systems shall remain operational in read-only mode until migration sign-off.
The System shall be deployed within the territory of Pakistan.

The primary site shall be the PITA Government Data Centre, with a disaster recovery site at a geographically separate in-country facility providing a recovery point objective (RPO) of no more than 15 minutes and a recovery time objective (RTO) of no more than 4 hours.
Citizen data shall not be stored, processed or replicated outside Pakistan under any circumstances.

The Bidder shall size, install and configure the runtime environment using the Authority-provided virtualised infrastructure, and shall implement environment separation for development, testing, staging and production.

The Bidder shall establish and operate a citizen facilitation helpdesk providing support in Urdu and English from 08:00 to 22:00 PKT, seven days a week, through telephone, email, web chat and an in-portal ticketing system.
The Bidder shall also provide second-line and third-line technical support for the System on a 24x7 basis for Severity 1 incidents.
The System shall achieve a monthly service availability of at least 99.9 percent, measured at the production application tier and excluding agreed maintenance windows, throughout the O&M Period.

The Bidder shall design and deliver a structured training programme covering: end-user training for at least 800 departmental officers across the Province; administrator and operations training for up to 40 PITA engineers; train-the-trainer sessions for 60 master trainers; and executive briefings for departmental leadership.

Training shall be delivered in a blended mode with classroom sessions in the provincial capital and divisional headquarters, e-learning modules hosted on the Portal, bilingual user manuals, and quick reference guides.
A comprehensive knowledge transfer and exit management plan shall be executed during the final six months of the O&M Period.
The Authority shall endeavour to adhere to the following schedule.
Any change shall be communicated to all prospective Bidders through an addendum posted on the Authority's website and the PPRA portal.

A pre-bid meeting shall be held on Tuesday, 30 June 2026 at 11:00 PKT in the PITA Auditorium, 3rd Floor, PITA Headquarters, Sector G-5, Provincial Capital City, with simultaneous participation available via Microsoft Teams.
Minutes of the pre-bid meeting and the Authority's responses to questions raised shall be circulated to all firms that have obtained the RFP and shall form an integral part of this RFP.
Questions received after this deadline shall not be entertained.
The Authority shall issue consolidated responses to all clarification questions by Thursday, 16 July 2026 without identifying the source of any question.
The Authority shall not be responsible for postal or courier delays under any circumstances.
Technical envelopes shall be opened publicly on the same day at 15:30 PKT in the presence of Bidders' representatives who choose to attend.
Each Bidder must satisfy all of the following mandatory eligibility criteria at the proposal submission deadline.
Compliance shall be established through the documentary evidence indicated against each criterion and recorded in the Eligibility Compliance Sheet (Annex B).

ME-1: The Bidder must be a company incorporated in Pakistan and registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP). Evidence: certificate of incorporation and latest Form-A/Form-29.
ME-2: The Bidder must hold a valid registration with the Pakistan Software Export Board (PSEB) for the current financial year. Evidence: valid PSEB registration certificate.

ME-3: The Bidder must be registered with the Federal Board of Revenue for income tax and sales tax and must appear on the Active Taxpayers List. Evidence: NTN certificate, STRN certificate and ATL printout.

ME-4: The Bidder must hold a valid ISO/IEC 27001 certification for information security management, covering its software development and operations facilities. Evidence: valid certificate issued by an accredited certification body.
ME-5: The Bidder must hold a valid ISO 22301 Business Continuity Management certification (mandatory). Evidence: valid certificate issued by an accredited certification body.

ME-6: The Bidder must hold a current CMMI Level 5 appraisal (mandatory) under CMMI-DEV v2.0 or later, published on the CMMI Institute PARS directory. Evidence: appraisal disclosure statement and PARS listing.

ME-7: The Bidder must have been in continuous operation in the software development business for at least five (5) years as of the date of issue of this RFP. Evidence: certificate of incorporation and financial statements.

ME-8: The Bidder must have successfully completed at least three (3) projects of a similar nature (web-based application development and implementation for government or large enterprise clients), each with a contract value of not less than PKR 50 million, within the last five (5) years. Evidence: contract copies or work orders together with satisfactory completion certificates from the clients.

ME-9: The Bidder must have an average annual turnover of at least PKR 150 million over the last three (3) audited financial years. Evidence: audited financial statements for the three most recent financial years.

ME-10: The Bidder must submit an affidavit on stamp paper, duly notarised, declaring that the firm is not blacklisted, debarred or suspended by any federal, provincial or local government entity, autonomous body or public procurement regulatory authority in Pakistan. Evidence: original affidavit.

ME-11: The Bidder must furnish bid security equal to two percent (2%) of the total bid price in the form prescribed in Section 10. Evidence: original bank guarantee or pay order enclosed with the financial envelope.

ME-12: The Bidder shall provide a written commitment, signed by its chief executive, to establish and staff an operational regional office in the provincial capital within 30 days of contract award (commitment), and to maintain that office for the full duration of the Contract. Evidence: signed letter of commitment on company letterhead.

A Bidder shall not be eligible if it was engaged by the Authority as a consultant for the preparation of the design, specifications or other documents forming part of this RFP, or if it is an affiliate of any such consultant.
TR-01: The System shall be designed on a modular, service-oriented or microservices architecture with documented APIs for every service module.
TR-02: The System shall expose all integration interfaces as versioned RESTful APIs secured with OAuth 2.0, and shall publish an internal API catalogue with machine-readable specifications.
TR-03: The System shall be deployable on the Authority's virtualised on-premises infrastructure without dependence on any proprietary public cloud service.

TR-04: The System shall support horizontal scaling to no fewer than 2,000 concurrent authenticated user sessions and 25,000 daily applications at full rollout, with a page response time not exceeding 3 seconds at the 95th percentile under peak load.
TR-05: The System shall use open standards for all stored documents and shall digitally sign issued certificates using PKI certificates from a licensed certification authority in Pakistan.

TR-06: The Portal shall provide bilingual content management in Urdu and English, with all citizen-facing screens, notifications, receipts and certificates rendered in the language selected by the user.
TR-07: The Portal shall conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, verified through an independent accessibility audit prior to Go-Live.
TR-08: The Portal shall provide a configurable forms engine permitting Authority administrators to create and modify service application forms, checklists and fee rules without vendor code changes.
TR-09: The Portal shall provide a citizen document wallet in which verified certificates and previously uploaded documents are reusable across services.
TR-10: The Portal shall provide dashboards and operational reports for each department, including service volumes, processing times, SLA breaches and revenue collected, with export to Excel and CSV.
TR-11: The System shall verify citizen identity against the national identity database through the Authority's existing verification gateway, and shall log every verification transaction.

TR-12: The System shall integrate with at least two licensed payment aggregators and shall support card, account-to-account, wallet and over-the-counter challan payments with automated end-of-day reconciliation.
TR-13: The System shall provide SMS and email notification services through the Authority's empanelled gateways, with delivery status tracking and configurable bilingual templates.
TR-14: The System shall integrate with the provincial land records, civil registration and treasury systems through the interface specifications provided in Annex E.

TR-15: The Bidder shall submit a detailed data migration strategy, including profiling results, cleansing and transformation rules, rehearsal plans and rollback procedures, for approval prior to the first migration wave.

TR-16: Each migration wave shall conclude with a reconciliation report demonstrating 100 percent record accountability, with discrepancies itemised and dispositioned in consultation with the data-owning department.

TR-17: The System shall implement role-based access control with segregation of duties, multi-factor authentication for all administrative accounts, and a tamper-evident audit trail of all create, update, delete and view operations on citizen records.
TR-18: The System shall encrypt all data in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and all sensitive data at rest using AES-256 or an equivalent approved algorithm.

TR-19: The Bidder shall arrange an independent vulnerability assessment and penetration test by a firm approved by the Authority before Go-Live and annually thereafter, and shall remediate all critical and high findings before public launch.

TR-20: The System and all associated operational processes shall comply with the Authority's Information Security Policy and applicable data protection legislation of Pakistan; citizen data shall be hosted exclusively within Pakistan.

TR-21: The Bidder shall appoint a dedicated, certified information security officer for the duration of the Contract and shall report security incidents to the Authority within four (4) hours of detection.

TR-22: The Bidder shall operate the helpdesk and technical support functions in accordance with ITIL-aligned incident, problem, change and release management processes, supported by a service management tool with ticket-level reporting.

TR-23: The System shall be monitored through an application performance monitoring toolset with automated alerting, and monthly SLA reports shall be submitted to the Authority within five (5) working days of month end.
TR-24: The Bidder shall maintain the System at vendor-supported versions of all third-party components throughout the O&M Period, applying security patches within the timelines defined in the SLA.
TR-25: The Bidder shall deliver the training programme described in Section 3.9 and shall achieve a post-training assessment pass rate of at least 80 percent among trained officers.

TR-26: The Bidder shall deliver and maintain complete documentation, including system design, API specifications, operations runbooks, administrator manuals and bilingual end-user guides, updated with every major release.

The System shall achieve a monthly availability of at least 99.9 percent during the O&M Period, measured at the production application tier, twenty-four hours a day, excluding scheduled maintenance windows agreed at least five (5) working days in advance and limited to a maximum of four (4) hours per calendar month between 00:00 and 06:00 PKT.

Incidents shall be classified and serviced according to the following matrix: Severity Definition Response Time Resolution Time Severity 1 Portal or payment services unavailable to all users 15 minutes 4 hours Severity 2 Major function degraded; no workaround available 30 minutes 8 hours Severity 3 Minor function impaired; workaround available 2 hours 3 working days Severity 4 Cosmetic issue or service request 8 hours 10 working days

draft.title: Relevant Experience & Past Performance
draft.content:
**Inland Revenue e-Filing Portal — Azad Jammu & Kashmir** [CAP-038] — AJK Inland Revenue Department (Government), 2025, USD 510k, 15 months.
Deployed a tailored instance of our revenue-collection platform for the AJK Inland Revenue Department, covering taxpayer registration, sales-tax e-filing, e-payments and arrears management with a bilingual Urdu/English taxpayer portal. Added a mobile inspection app for field officers with offline assessment capture. Conducted taxpayer-facilitation drives and trained 160 departmental users as part of capacity building. _Outcome: First e-filing season closed with 74% electronic returns; revenue collection grew 19% year-on-year; manual challan errors eliminated at participating banks._

**Federal e-Procurement System Enhancement & Rollout** [CAP-036] — Federal Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (Government), 2024, USD 1300k, 28 months.
National-scale follow-on to our provincial e-procurement build: enhanced the federal e-procurement platform with framework agreements, reverse auctions, supplier performance scoring and open-contracting (OCDS) data publication. Onboarded 280 federal procuring agencies with structured change management, bilingual training academies and a 24/7 supplier helpdesk. Security hardened to ISO 27001 controls with annual third-party VAPT. _Outcome: Federal tender publication compliance reached 97%; average savings of 12% recorded on reverse-auction categories; OCDS portal cited in international transparency review._

**Vehicle Registration & Excise Management System** [CAP-037] — Provincial Excise, Taxation & Narcotics Control Department (Government), 2024, USD 640k, 16 months.
Adapted our license-management platform for motor vehicle registration, transfer and token tax collection across 30 excise offices, with biometric owner verification, online tax calculators and doorstep number-plate delivery tracking. Integrated e-payment channels and a public vehicle-verification SMS/web service used by buyers and law enforcement. Provided staff training and a 3-year managed support arrangement with 99.5% availability SLA. _Outcome: Vehicle transfer turnaround cut from 21 days to 4 days; token tax collection up 33% after online channels launched; 2.6 million verification queries served annually._

**Online Tax Filing & Revenue Collection Portal** [CAP-006] — Provincial Revenue Authority (Government), 2023, USD 880k, 22 months.
Replaced manual sales-tax-on-services filing with an online portal for taxpayer registration, e-filing of monthly returns, e-payments via 1Link/ADC channels and risk-based audit case selection. Built taxpayer ledgers, withholding statements, refund workflows and a business-intelligence layer for revenue forecasting. The platform passed an independent VAPT, operates under ISO 27001-aligned ISMS controls, and is supported by a 24/7 bilingual helpdesk with a 99.9% uptime SLA during filing windows. _Outcome: Registered taxpayer base grew 42%; on-time filing compliance improved from 61% to 88%; collections increased 27% year-on-year after launch._

**Citizen e-Services Portal Phase II — Khyber Pakhtunkhwa** [CAP-034] — Provincial Information Technology Board (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) (Government), 2023, USD 780k, 20 months.
Follow-on engagement replicating and extending our citizen facilitation portal for a second province, expanding the catalogue to 120 bilingual Urdu/English e-services with a unified citizen wallet for fee payments and WCAG 2.1 AA accessible design. Added an API gateway so other departments can publish services onto the platform under a shared single sign-on. Operated under a 99.9% uptime SLA with 24/7 monitoring from our Islamabad NOC. _Outcome: 1.9 million citizen registrations in year one; 86% of targeted services fully online; service-center footfall reduced 39% in pilot districts._

**Provincial e-Procurement Platform (e-Tendering & Supplier Registration)** [CAP-003] — Provincial Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (Government), 2022, USD 1100k, 30 months.
Built and rolled out an end-to-end e-procurement platform covering supplier registration, e-tendering, online bid submission with PKI digital signatures and encryption, two-envelope bid evaluation workflows, contract award publication and grievance handling. The system enforces procurement rules engines per PPRA regulations and produces complete audit logs for accountability bodies. Operated a 24/7 bidder helpdesk with bilingual Urdu/English support and ran capacity-building workshops for 1,800 suppliers and 350 procuring-entity officers. _Outcome: 4,100 tenders processed worth USD 700M in first two years; average tender cycle shortened by 31%; supplier participation per tender up from 3.1 to 5.8 bids._
